description:
Plan: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-exceptions.html, decisions 1-3, ticket 1. Keystone of the epic.

Build: (a) Process gains a handler stack (runtime/src/process.rs), a GC root beside runnable and the mailbox on JIT and AOT; the interpreter marks a handler frame on its Vec<BackendContinuation>. (b) fz_panic (runtime/src/failure.rs) delivers (kind=error, value) to the top handler when one is active: pops it, materialises the handler closure with the kind and value as arguments, sets runnable, returns; the caller unwinds as today (native returns 0 to the trampoline; the interpreter pops frames to the marker). With no handler it is today's route, unchanged. (c) end_failed_process's post-condition becomes "failed, or a handler is runnable"; neither still traps. (d) try lowers in src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs as one step: body block, handler template (outer continuation + captures), a dispatch over (kind, __struct__) built from the rescue heads, miss row re-raises, one join value typed as the union of body and arms. The body's continuation pops the handler and delivers to the join, so body calls are non-tail by construction and body bindings do not reach the join. (e) The five Elixir rescue shapes and only those: e, Alias, [A, B], e in Alias, e in [A, B]; anything else is the compile error Elixir gives ("invalid rescue clause ..."). ErlangError matches a non-struct value and binds %ErlangError{original: value}. (f) try with none of rescue/catch/after is a compile error with Elixir's text; the catch, after and else keys are refused with a plain "not yet supported" diagnostic until fz-3ul.2 and fz-3ul.3 add them. (g) Telemetry: process_exited gains raises_delivered; a fz.runtime.raise event carries kind, exception name, handler depth.

Acceptance (all on interp, run and build; expected output produced by running elixir on the oracle):
- rescue by alias; rescue by list; e in Alias binding e and reading e.message; bare e; rescue ErlangError of panic(:badarg); rescue ArgumentError of raise ArgumentError, "x".
- nested try: inner handler wins; an arm set that does not match re-raises to the outer try; an uncaught raise after a try completed normally still prints the line and exits 1 (the handler was popped).
- a raise inside a rescue arm is not caught by the same try.
- body value flows to the join when nothing raises; the try's value is usable (dbg(try ... end)).
- a try in a spawned process rescues; main continues.
- a try in a 100_000-iteration tail loop where every iteration raises and rescues: finishes, exit 0, reductions yield at least once (handler stack survives a mid-flight yield and GC).
- fixture asserts raises_delivered through the exit-record telemetry, and a fz.runtime.raise event is observable in a Rust test.
- unit tests in sibling _test.rs files: handler push/pop/delivery in the runtime; interpreter marker frame; the rescue-shape diagnostics.
- .agent/docs/process-failure.md rewritten as the exceptions doc (handler stack, delivery contract, kinds, empty-stack case); fixtures.md gains the rescue forms; docs.md index line updated.
- gate green: RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets, doc tests, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check. No pin or golden rises without a measured explanation.
